block.txt: An Act to incorporate the Principal and Councillors of Sancta Sophia College; to establish Sancta Sophia College as a College of and within the University; to vest certain lands in the University and to empower the University to grant such lands to Trustees for the purposes of Sancta Sophia College; to vest certain lands held by trustees in trust for the rector and Fellows of Saint John’s College in certain other persons; to amend the University and University Colleges Act 1900, and certain other Acts; and for purposes connected therewith.
This Act may be cited as the Sancta Sophia College Incorporation Act 1929.
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
Body corporate means the Principal and Councillors of Sancta Sophia College, incorporated under this Act.
College means Sancta Sophia Hall established as a college of the University by this Act.
Sancta Sophia Hall means the building erected on the land described in Schedule 1.

So soon as the Governor is satisfied that a principal and eighteen councillors for the government of Sancta Sophia Hall in accordance with the constitution thereof, as in this Act set forth, have been duly appointed and elected respectively, the same shall be notified by the Governor by proclamation in the Gazette.
For notification under this subsection, see Gazette No 28 of 7.3.1930, p 1119.

Immediately upon such notification and from thenceforth the principal and councillors of Sancta Sophia Hall shall be and they are hereby constituted a body corporate by the name of “The Principal and Councillors of Sancta Sophia College”, by which name the body corporate shall sue and be sued or otherwise appear, answer, and be answered.
The body corporate shall have perpetual succession and a common seal.

The body corporate may take and hold them or their successors by grant, will, or otherwise in perpetuity, or for any term of life or years, as well chattels and other personal property as land, buildings, and other hereditaments, and subject to subsection (5) alien or otherwise dispose of or demise the same or any part thereof.

It shall not be lawful for the body corporate or any person or persons seised of or entitled to any lands in trust for the body corporate or for the purposes of the college to alienate, mortgage, charge, or demise any lands or hereditaments granted to or in trust for the body corporate or for college purposes by His Majesty or his successors or by the University of Sydney without the consent in writing of the Governor.
The body corporate may do all other things incident or appertaining to a body corporate.

heading.b: Principal and councillors to constitute a council

block.txt: The body corporate is to consist of a principal and 15 councillors, of whom 3 are to be duly approved priests of the Roman Catholic Church in New South Wales.
The councillors shall appoint the principal, who shall not be one of themselves.
The principal and councillors for the time being shall together form a council to be called “The Council of Sancta Sophia College”.
The government in every respect of the college and all matters relating thereto shall at all times be vested in the council.
The Roman Catholic Archbishop of Sydney shall be Visitor of the college with all such powers as by law appertain to the office of Visitor of a college.

The council shall have power to appoint for such term as they think fit one or more vice-principal or vice-principals who in order of seniority of appointment shall in the principal’s absence have all the powers and discharge all the duties of the principal.

The principal and vice-principals shall be respectively liable to removal or suspension for sufficient cause by the councillors subject to appeal to the Visitor in the manner prescribed by the by-laws.

Any vacancy in the office of councillor shall be supplied, in such manner as may be prescribed by the by-laws, by the remaining councillors and those members of the college who are graduates of the University continuing on the books of the college.

heading.b: Sancta Sophia Hall to be a college of and within the University

block.txt: Sancta Sophia College shall be a college of and within the University of Sydney.

All students in the college shall immediately upon entering the college matriculate in the said University and shall thereafter continue to be members thereof and submit and be subject to the discipline thereof and shall be required duly and regularly to attend the lectures of the University on those subjects an examination and proficiency in which are required for honours or degrees.

The council of the college shall have power from time to time to make and establish all such by-laws and rules for carrying into effect the several provisions and objects of this Act as the council deems fit and particularly:
for declaring the causes which shall create vacancies in the office of councillors, and
directing who shall preside at meetings of the council and of the councillors, and
for the management of the college, and
prescribing the duties of the several officers thereof and of the principal and vice-principals, and
the ordering of all things in and connected with the college and the discipline thereof.

Every such by-law and rule shall be transmitted to the Governor within thirty days after being made, to be by him laid before both the Houses of Parliament of the State as soon as conveniently may be thereafter.
The principal or vice-principal of the college, subject only to the by-laws and rules so made, shall have the general superintendence and control of the students and of the institution.

The votes at all meetings of the council (except votes for the appointment of a principal) shall be taken exclusively of the person presiding unless there shall be an equality of votes, in which case he or she shall have a casting vote.

In every case where all the councillors entitled to attend shall have had notice of the time and place of intended meeting, 6 members of the council with the principal shall constitute a meeting of the council, and the votes and proceedings of the majority at any such meeting shall be taken and accepted as the votes and proceedings of the council or councillors respectively.

heading.b: Temporary vacancies not to prejudice the corporation

block.txt: No temporary vacancy or vacancies in the office of principal or in the number of councillors shall be deemed in any way to affect the constitution of the college or its privileges or status as a body corporate.

heading.b: Vesting in University of land described in Schedule 1

block.txt: The land described in Schedule 1 shall be and the same is hereby vested in the University of Sydney their successors and assigns for an estate in fee simple to be held freed from any trusts in favour of the Rector and Fellows of St. John’s College but subject to the trusts mentioned in section 16.

heading.b: Vesting in University of land described in Schedule 2

block.txt: The land described in Schedule 2 shall be and the same is hereby vested in the University of Sydney their successors and assigns for an estate in fee simple to be held freed from any of the trusts declared in Crown grant dated the sixth day of January, one thousand eight hundred and eighty, volume four hundred and eighty-six, folio one hundred and thirty-five, and Crown grant dated the tenth day of December, one thousand eight hundred and ninety-nine, volume four hundred and eighty-eight, folio one hundred and thirteen, respectively, but subject to the trusts mentioned in section 16.

The land described in Schedule 3 being the whole of the land contained in Schedule 1 and the whole of the land contained in Schedule 2 and hereby vested in the University of Sydney shall be held upon trust to make and execute a subgrant of such land upon trust for the body corporate in the same manner and with the same effect in all respects as of such land were part of one of four several portions consisting of not less than eighteen acres, directed by the Crown grant of land to the University of Sydney dated the eighteenth day of January, one thousand eight hundred and fifty-five, to be selected by the Senate of the said University for the purposes in the said Crown grant declared and as if such portion had lapsed so far as regards such part and as if the Governor with the advice of the Executive Council and after such lapse had nominated the Sancta Sophia Hall as a College in trust for which land or lands so set apart as aforesaid were to be subgranted subject to the provisions by the said Crown grant directed in the case of any such subgrant.

heading.b: Vesting in Trustees of land described in Schedule 4

block.txt: The land described in Schedule 4 is hereby vested in the Most Reverend Michael Kelly, Roman Catholic Archbishop of Sydney; the Most Reverend Michael Sheehan, coadjutor Archbishop of Sydney; the Right Reverend Monsignor Patrick Lewis Coonan of Forest Lodge, Rector General; the Very Reverend Thomas Phelan of Lewisham, Chancellor; and the Reverend Thomas Gabriel Kelleher of Camperdown, Clerk in Holy Orders, for an estate in fee simple as joint tenants to be held freed from any trusts in favour of the University of Sydney and Rector and Fellows of St. John’s College, and as if such land were part of the land granted by Crown grant, dated the sixth day of January, one thousand eight hundred and eighty, volume four hundred and eighty-six, folio one hundred and thirty-four.

heading.b: Modification of subgrant to St. John’s College

block.txt: From and after the passing of this Act the subgrant of land by the University of Sydney to trustees for the Rector and Fellows of St. John’s College, dated the fifth day of December, one thousand eight hundred and sixty, shall be read and construed as if the land thereby subgranted had been the land described in Schedule 5 and as if the plan endorsed thereon had been omitted therefrom. In all other respects the said subgrant is hereby ratified and confirmed.
